decisions.difference: A: impaction task triggered by (and Constipation (or Bed-ridden, Seen by palliative care service, Chronic constipation with overflow))  vs  B: impaction task triggered by Constipation alone, with the gate findings in its check_for
decisions.final_expr: (and (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Constipation" "finding")) (or Bed-ridden, Seen by palliative care service, Chronic constipation with overflow))
decisions.reason: The page says "If > 65 years, bed-bound/receiving palliative care, or overflow diarrhoea, check for solid immobile bulk of stool in rectum", so the rectal check is conditional on the gate.

decisions.difference: A: colorectal cancer symptom task triggered by Constipation  vs  B: no such task
decisions.reason: "Assess the patient with constipation for colorectal cancer … Ask about common colorectal cancer symptoms" is an instruction to check every constipated patient.

decisions.difference: A: Obstipation in the urgent task  vs  B: not checked
decisions.reason: It is the evidence for "No stools … in the past 24 hours" in the urgent rule (see priority decision), so it must be checked for.

decisions.difference: A: Bed-ridden, Seen by palliative care service, Chronic constipation with overflow in the urgent task  vs  B: in the impaction task
decisions.final_expr: (Bed-ridden, Seen by palliative care service, Chronic constipation with overflow in check_for of "Check for urgent constipation conditions")
decisions.reason: Because the impaction task is gated on these findings ("If > 65 years, bed-bound/receiving palliative care, or overflow diarrhoea, check …"), they have to be asked about in the always-on constipation task.

decisions.difference: A: Chronic constipation with overflow (disorder)  vs  B: Spurious diarrhea - overflow (finding)
decisions.reason: The page defines overflow diarrhoea as "prolonged constipation followed by watery stool"; A's concept is a kind of Chronic constipation and Chronic diarrhea, while B's sits under Incontinence of feces.

decisions.difference: A: colorectal cancer symptoms (Diarrhea, Rectal hemorrhage, Hematochezia, Abdominal discomfort, Abdominal colic, Flatulence symptom, Tenesmus of anus and/or rectum, Unexplained weight loss, Asthenia, Fatigue)  vs  B: none
decisions.final_expr: (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Diarrhea" "finding")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Rectal hemorrhage" "disorder")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Hematochezia" "finding")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Abdominal discomfort" "finding")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Abdominal colic" "finding")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Flatulence symptom" "finding")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Tenesmus of anus and/or rectum" "finding")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Unexplained weight loss" "finding")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Asthenia" "finding")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Fatigue" "finding"))
decisions.reason: The page lists these as the symptoms to "Ask about": "diarrhoea", "Rectal bleeding or visible blood in stool", "abdominal discomfort including cramps, gas or pain", "tenesmus", "Unexplained weight loss/weakness/fatigue".

decisions.difference: A: (>= (onset Obstipation) (time_ago 24 hours)) plus Constipation  vs  B: (>= (onset Constipation) (time_ago 24 hours))
decisions.reason: "No stools … in the past 24 hours" describes a complete absence of stool, which Obstipation is closer to than constipation that began 24 hours ago; neither concept says "no stools" exactly.

decisions.difference: A: (diagnosis Malignant neoplasm of cecum and/or colon and/or rectum possible)  vs  B: none
decisions.final_expr: (diagnosis (snomed_concept "Malignant neoplasm of cecum and/or colon and/or rectum" "disorder") possible)
decisions.reason: The section is headed "Assess the patient with constipation for colorectal cancer" and ends "If patient has any of above symptoms, discuss/refer", which reads as suspecting colorectal cancer, but the page never says "consider" or "likely".

decisions.difference: A: possible colorectal cancer evidence = Constipation and (any listed symptom, incl. Abdominal pain)  vs  B: none
decisions.final_expr: (and Constipation (or Diarrhea, Rectal hemorrhage, Hematochezia, Abdominal discomfort, Abdominal colic, Flatulence symptom, Abdominal pain, Tenesmus of anus and/or rectum, Unexplained weight loss, Asthenia, Fatigue))
decisions.reason: "If patient has any of above symptoms" is an or over the listed symptoms, and "cramps, gas or pain" includes abdominal pain; follows the diagnosis decision above.

decisions.difference: A: impaction gate uses Chronic constipation with overflow  vs  B: Spurious diarrhea - overflow
decisions.reason: Same as the check_for decision: the page's definition is "prolonged constipation followed by watery stool".

notes: Both builds passed. A was taken as base: it encodes the gated impaction check the page describes and the colorectal cancer assessment section; B left the colorectal section out. Shared choices kept: neither-stools-nor-flatus reading, Unable to break wind, Hard stool + Rectum structure for the rectal bulk, Seen by palliative care service, '> 65 years' and '> 50 years' not representable, Hb/TSH not modelled. B's questions on the Constipation-onset alternative and on whether the colorectal section should be a diagnosis at all are merged into the remaining questions. The urgent task's check_for also carries the impaction gate findings (bed-bound, palliative care, overflow) because the impaction task is gated on them.
